title: Grade 6 Science — Thu, Jun 19
description: Changes Around Us — Day 4 of 5: Rusting — conditions and prevention
subject: science

questions.question: Rusting of iron requires ___.
questions.explanation: Iron rusts only when both water (moisture) and oxygen are present. Remove either one and rusting stops.

questions.question: Rust is chemically known as ___.
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O). It is reddish-brown in colour.

questions.question: If iron is stored in a completely dry environment (no moisture), it will ___.
questions.explanation: Without water (moisture), rusting cannot occur. Dry conditions prevent rusting.

questions.question: If iron is stored in air from which all oxygen has been removed, it will ___.
questions.explanation: Without oxygen, the rusting reaction cannot take place. Iron does not rust in the absence of oxygen.

questions.question: Painting an iron surface prevents rusting by ___.
options: Preventing contact of iron with water and oxygen
questions.explanation: Paint forms a barrier that prevents water and oxygen from reaching the iron surface, stopping rusting.

questions.question: Galvanizing is the process of coating iron with ___.
questions.explanation: Galvanization involves coating iron or steel with a layer of zinc to protect it from rusting.

questions.question: Why does zinc protect iron from rusting (galvanization)?
options: Zinc rusts instead of iron — sacrificial protection
questions.explanation: Zinc corrodes (oxidizes) preferentially instead of iron — called sacrificial protection. Even if scratched, the zinc protects the iron underneath.

questions.question: Oiling iron tools prevents rusting by ___.
options: Forming a layer that repels water and air
questions.explanation: Oil forms a thin protective layer that repels water and keeps oxygen away from the iron surface.

questions.question: Stainless steel does not rust because it contains ___.
options: Chromium (which forms a protective oxide layer)
questions.explanation: Stainless steel contains chromium, which forms a thin chromium oxide layer on the surface, protecting it from corrosion.

questions.question: Rusting is a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Rusting produces iron oxide (a new substance) — it is a chemical change. The original iron cannot easily be restored — it is irreversible.

questions.question: Which method is NOT used to prevent rusting?
questions.explanation: Keeping iron wet actually promotes rusting (water is one of the requirements). The other three are anti-rusting methods.

questions.question: Iron pipes carrying water tend to rust faster because ___.
options: They are in constant contact with water and dissolved oxygen
They are made of different iron
questions.explanation: Water pipes are constantly in contact with water (and dissolved oxygen), providing both conditions needed for rusting.

questions.question: Electroplating iron with chromium prevents rusting because ___.
options: Chromium forms a hard, corrosion-resistant coating
questions.explanation: Chromium electroplating creates a hard, shiny, corrosion-resistant layer that keeps iron away from moisture and oxygen.

questions.question: Ships are prone to rust because they are ___.
options: Constantly exposed to air and moisture (especially seawater)
questions.explanation: Ships are exposed to moisture, oxygen, and salt water — ideal conditions for rusting.

questions.question: The reddish-brown colour of rust is due to ___.
options: Iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) — formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water
questions.explanation: Rust is iron oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), which has a characteristic reddish-brown colour.
